newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia central bank acts to stem ringgit fall.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia central bank acts to stem ringgit fall.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia on Wednesday intervened in the interbank foreign exchange market to stem the ringgit's fall, dealers said.
They said the central bank came in to sell $100-200 million at 2.5120 a dollar. Its selling lasted until ringgit came down to 2.5100, with a bulk of the sales around 2.5110, they said.
There was no confirmation from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market intervention operations.
"The central bank was acting through some large Malaysian banks. The intention seems to just slow down the ringgit's fall, not stop it," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
Immediately after the intervention, the ringgit recovered 50 points to around 2.5060/70 a dollar. At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5080/90.
Support from the central bank also brought in Malaysian exporters, who had been waiting for dollar/ringgit's rise to sell their dollars, dealers said.
"Speculators who had been buying dollar/ringgit this morning also started squaring up as soon as they heard selling from Kuala Lumpur side," said a dealer with another Malaysian bank.
"This exaggerated the volumes after intervention," he said.
However, the strength of dollar/majors would not allow a major correction in dollar/ringgit, which has risen nearly 200 points in the last two days, dealers said.
In the morning, dollar/ringgit broke through 2.51/dollar, triggering stop-loss selling, due to which ringgit was expected to decline further.
A U.S. hedge fund, squaring up a large three-month position in the ringgit, was said to be responsible for the Malaysian currency's decline.
